selector.why: The evidence of a malignant small round blue cell tumor and molecular studies consistent with Ewing sarcoma/primitive neuroectodermal tumor decided it

frontier_selector.why: The evidence of a malignant small round blue cell tumor and molecular studies consistent with Ewing sarcoma/primitive neuroectodermal tumor decided it

support_spans: history of a 5 mm‐thick melanoma on his posterior neck
supporting_evidence: history of a 5 mm‐thick melanoma on his posterior neck

support_spans: Endobronchial ultrasound–guided fine-needle aspiration of the lung lesion demonstrated a malignant small round blue cell tumor
Molecular studies were negative for an EWSR1 translocation but otherwise were interpreted as consistent with Ewing sarcoma/primitive neuroectodermal tumor (PNET)
malignant small round blue cell tumor
contradict_spans: development of right neck adenopathy and interval growth of the hyoid bone lesion, suggesting a distinct pathology
A multidisciplinary sarcoma tumor board concluded that the hyoid lesion most likely represented a synchronous primary bone tumor (e.g., plasmacytoma, chondrosarcoma, or osteosarcoma)

support_spans: an intensely FDG-avid, partially calcified 4.1 × 2.3 × 2.8 cm expansile lesion within the right hyoid bone
contradict_spans: Molecular studies were negative for an EWSR1 translocation but otherwise were interpreted as consistent with Ewing sarcoma/primitive neuroectodermal tumor (PNET)
Ultrasound–guided core needle biopsy of the hyoid lesion was nondiagnostic, yielding only rare atypical epithelial cells amidst lymphocytes
